t: You're at St Bartholomew the Less, an Anglican church standing within the precincts of St Bartholomew's Hospital, in the City of London. It was once a parish church, and since June 2015 it has been a chapel of ease in the parish of St Bartholomew the Great. Several people are buried here. John Lyly, the Elizabethan playwright, wrote Euphues and gave his name to the style called euphuism. Thomas Watson, the poet and translator, pioneered the English madrigal, and Shakespeare was once called Watson's heir. The Scottish physician and botanist William Pitcairn is buried here too.
